title: edge-retail-kiosk-offline-pilot-engagement-outline
content:
Objective:
Deliver a 6-week pilot to evaluate a Redwood-hosted + on-prem hybrid inference setup for XPress Retail’s self-service kiosks. The pilot focuses on enabling low-latency conversational product lookup and offline fallback behavior when the kiosk loses connectivity. The goal is to validate latency SLOs, on-device model compatibility (quantized), model fallbacks, and an operations handoff plan for scaling to 500 stores.

Scope (what we'll deliver):
- Week 0: Kickoff & environment prep (accounts, access, sample data ingest)
- Week 1–2: Model onboarding and quantization experiments (redwood-compat variants + 4-bit quantized candidate)
- Week 2–3: Edge runtime integration on reference kiosk hardware (NVIDIA Jetson Xavier NX + local CPU fallback)
- Week 3–4: Connectivity-resilience behaviors: prefix/KV cache persistence, offline prompt routing, and lightweight summarization for degraded mode
- Week 4–5: Usability workshop with store ops and curated evals using real support transcripts
- Week 5–6: Final performance report, SLO verification, and production roadmap + cost model for Dedicated/Private options

Deliverables:
- Architecture diagram (hosted control plane + edge inference nodes)
- Quantization & perf matrix (latency, peak tokens/sec, memory) for 3 candidate model configs
- Integration guide for kiosk runtime (systemd service, model loading, cache persistence)
- Workshop notes + prioritized feature backlog for MLP/OPS handoff
- Pilot SLOs + regression tests (token-level cost estimations, latency percentiles)
- Executive summary & proposed commercial terms for scaling

High-level architecture assumptions:
- Control plane (Redwood Private) runs in customer's VPC for metadata and orchestration; inference workloads run locally on kiosk hardware for low-latency interactions.
- Model weights can be stored encrypted on-device; KMS integration for keys during deployment.
- Intermittent connectivity: the kiosk will operate fully offline for up to 12 hours and sync telemetry and cache on reconnect.

Reference hardware (customer-provided):
- Primary: Jetson Xavier NX, 8GB RAM, 1x NVMe 128GB (recommended)
- Alternate: Intel i7-based mini-PC with 16GB RAM (CPU fallback)
- Network: Cellular backup (4G/5G) + store WiFi

Key success criteria (pilot):
- 95th percentile response latency <= 400ms for cached prompts, <= 1.2s for cold-starts on quantized model
- Offline fallback returns meaningful, non-hallucinated answers 90% of the time on targeted eval prompts
- Model memory usage < 6GB after quantization and caching strategies on reference hardware
- Clear upgrade path to Dedicated capacity with predictable unit cost within 30% of hosted baseline

Staffing & roles (Redwood):
- Solutions lead (Aisha) — technical PM + primary customer liaison (0.2 FTE during pilot)
- Applied ML engineer (Diego) — quantization experiments, evals (1.0 FTE weeks 1–3)
- Edge integration engineer (Lena) — runtime packaging, kiosk onboarding (0.8 FTE weeks 2–5)
- Customer-facing SRE (Omar) — deployment runbooks and incident sims (0.3 FTE)
- Workshop facilitator (Priya) — ops training + playbook creation (0.2 FTE)

Estimated Pilot Costs (high-level sketch for proposal):
- Professional services: 6 weeks x blended rate $1,900/day -> $46,800 (includes travel & workshop prep)
- Engineering time (overhead & license): $7,200
- Edge validation hardware stipend (one-off): $3,000
- Optional: On-prem private control plane setup (one-time): $18,000
- Total pilot ask (recommended list price): $75,000 (negotiable based on commitment to scaling)

Commercial options post-pilot (packaging):
1) Redwood Dedicated Add-on: reserved inference capacity for model serving in region + hybrid routing to edge nodes. Annual commit recommended.
2) Hybrid Private: VPC control plane + managed edge release tooling, with support SLA for kiosk fleet.
3) Turnkey Edge: Redwood-managed appliance image, quarterly firmware updates, and model ops retainers.

Pricing heuristics we used (notes to sales):
- PS rates assume on-site workshop days are billed fully; remote days are discounted at 40%
- Hardware stipend covers procurement of one reference unit and smoke-test accessories
- Private control plane one-time includes KMS integration and audit log retention for 90 days

Workshop agenda (half-day on site):
- 09:00 — Kickoff & goals alignment (30m)
- 09:30 — System walkthrough: control plane, edge runtime, and data flows (45m)
- 10:15 — Quantization demo & perf tradeoffs (30m)
- 10:45 — Break (15m)
- 11:00 — Failure modes tabletop (30m)
- 11:30 — Ops handoff: deployment runbook + config templating (30m)
- 12:00 — Prioritization + next steps (30m)

Open questions / risks (we should clarify before SOW sign):
- Does XPress Retail permit on-device storage of model artifacts (legal/policy)? Who signs the AUP?
- Expected daily interaction volume per kiosk (peak and tail) -> affects Dedicated sizing
- Regulatory constraints for PII in transcripts (will require redaction or token-level retention)
- Hardware variance across stores (we need at least 75% of stores matching the reference spec for pilot validity)

Quick TODOs (owner):
- [ ] Confirm legal on-device model storage (Aisha)
- [ ] Collect sample transcripts and product catalog export (Customer)
- [ ] Provision staging VPC and service account for pilot (Omar)
- [ ] Create Confluence page for quantization results and scripts (Diego)
- [ ] Draft SOW contract template and payment milestones (Priya)

Acceptance & milestones (proposed payment schedule):
- 25% at SOW signing
- 40% after week 3 (integration + perf baseline delivery)
- 35% after final report and handoff

Appendix: quick perf checklist to run on reference unit (for engineering):
- Boot & verify NVMe throughput >= 600 MB/s
- Model load time (cold) < 5s for quantized bin
- Sustained token generation >= 8 tokens/sec at 20-token context
- KV cache warmup latency < 100ms

Notes from internal sync (2026-02-26):
- Customer prefers a hybrid contract that allows switching between Dedicated and Private after 6 months with a simple repricing clause.
- Solution team raised concern about telemetry volume and retention; recommend 30-day default with option to extend.
- Proposed next step: 1-page commercial brief for account team by EOW (Aisha + Priya).

Unresolved: scope of human-in-the-loop moderation during pilot — suggest minimal manual review for edge errors and an automated sampling pipeline for quality metrics.

If approved, next immediate actions: 1) share SOW draft with legal, 2) schedule kickoff with customer, 3) procure reference hardware and sign NDA addendum for on-device model storage.
